root_idea.summary: The root centers on mockery: treating a person, thing, message, or sign as an object of ridicule or derision.
root_idea.development: The basic sense of mocking develops in Quranic usage into the Form X expression for engaging in mockery. In the specific divine construction الله يستهزئ بهم, it denotes requital through apparent respite and eventual sudden seizure, rather than ordinary human mockery.

senses.definition: To mock, ridicule, scoff at, or deride a person or thing.
senses.usage_conditions: Used for active and passive constructions of engaging in or being subjected to mockery; the Quranic usage includes mockery directed toward messengers, signs, revelation, or other persons.

senses.definition: In the divine construction “God mocks them,” to requite their mockery by leaving them in delusion for a time and then taking them unexpectedly.
senses.usage_conditions: A Quran-specific figurative and retaliatory use, explained as a form of entrapment or requital rather than literal human mockery.

senses.definition: Mockery, ridicule, or jesting treatment; something treated as an object of derision.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quran uses it in constructions such as taking a person, sign, revelation, or matter as mockery or jest, including اتخذ ... هزواً. The term can denote joking and conduct resembling joking, especially when used to belittle what is being discussed.

senses.definition: One who mocks, ridicules, or treats others as objects of derision; a mocker.
senses.usage_conditions: A substantivized active participle of اِسْتَهْزَأَ; the Quranic occurrences are plural and refer to people characterized by this conduct.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To mock, scoff at, laugh at, deride, or ridicule someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Form I verb is reported with بِهِ and, in some usage, مِنْهُ.
A Classical Form I use, including the breaking of arrowheads in a poetic expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause death by severe cold.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported of killing camels or a person by cold; the attribution is explicitly considered possibly confused with هَرَأَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put a ridden beast in motion or excite it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical use applied to the beast on which one rides.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To die suddenly, unexpectedly, or on the spot.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported of dying in one's place or immediately.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To enter upon a period of severe cold.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare Form IV use, explicitly associated with the commonly used form أَهْرَأَ as a possible alternative or correction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a she-camel, to hasten with her rider.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the construction اهزأت به ناقته.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who is mocked, derided, or regarded as ridiculous.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun naming the object or victim of mockery.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who mocks, scoffs at, laughs at, or derides others.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun naming the agent of mockery.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the expression غَدَاةٌ هَازِئَةٌ, a morning of intense cold.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tropical expression describing cold that makes people shrug and shiver as though mocked.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the expression مَفَازَةٌ هَازِئَةٌ بِالرَّكْبِ, a desert that frustrates or “mocks” travelers.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tropical personification of a desert that impedes a company of riders.
